info.name: pt-orchestrator — Jenkins Workflow
info.description: 3-step collection: Register a YAML workflow → Trigger it → Monitor Jenkins job progress continuously.

body.raw:
id: jenkins_test-failure
version: "1.0"
name: Test Jenkins Failure Handling - Division by Zero
stages:
  - id: test-failure-scenario
    executionMode: SEQUENTIAL
    steps:
      - id: trigger-division-by-zero
        type: JENKINS_JOB
        config:
          jenkinsUrl: "${JENKINS_URL:http://localhost:9090}"
          jobName: "calculator-pipeline"
          username: "${JENKINS_USER:pt-orch}"
          token: "${JENKINS_TOKEN}"
          parameters:
            OPERATION: "DIVIDE"
            NUM1: "100"
            NUM2: "0"
            VERBOSE: "true"

      - id: should-not-execute
        type: JENKINS_JOB
        config:
          jenkinsUrl: "${JENKINS_URL:http://localhost:9090}"
          jobName: "calculator-pipeline"
          username: "${JENKINS_USER:pt-orch}"
          token: "${JENKINS_TOKEN}"
          parameters:
            OPERATION: "ADD"
            NUM1: "1"
            NUM2: "1"
            VERBOSE: "false"

request.description:
Registers (or re-registers) a YAML workflow definition.

Paste any valid workflow YAML in the body. On re-register, step configs are updated in-place even if the workflow has prior runs.

The workflowId is auto-saved to the WORKFLOW_ID collection variable.

exec: console.log('✅ Registered: ' + json.workflowId + ' — ready to trigger');

request.description:
Triggers a new execution of the workflow in WORKFLOW_ID.

The orchestrator immediately queues the Jenkins job and starts polling it. The runId is auto-saved to RUN_ID — use Step 3 to monitor.

exec: console.log('🚀 Triggered run: ' + json.runId + ' — initial status: ' + json.status);
console.log('Now send Step 3 to monitor progress...');

request.description:
Polls the orchestrator for the current Jenkins job status.

use the Collection Runner to poll automatically:
  Runner → select this request → Iterations: 60, Delay: 5000ms

The script auto-loops via setNextRequest while the job is running, and stops on SUCCESS or FAILED.

exec: console.log('[' + ts + '] Jenkins job status: ' + status);
pm.test('✅ Jenkins job completed successfully', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);
console.log('🎉 Done! Run finished at ' + json.endTime);
console.log('⏳ Still ' + status + ' — polling again in 5s...');
